docs.title: Contributing to PowerCV
docs.text: Thank you for considering contributing to PowerCV! This document outlines the guidelines for contributing to the project.

docs.title: How to Contribute
docs.text:
1. Fork the repository and create a new branch for your feature or bugfix.
  2. Make your changes, ensuring they follow the project's coding standards.
  3. Write tests for your changes and ensure all tests pass.
  4. Submit a pull request with a clear description of your changes.

docs.title: Coding Standards
docs.text:
• Follow PEP 8 for Python code.
  • Use type annotations and docstrings.
  • Write meaningful commit messages (see CONTRIBUTING.md for examples).

docs.title: Reporting Issues
docs.text: If you encounter any issues, please report them by creating a new issue in the GitHub repository. Provide as much detail as possible, including steps to reproduce the issue.

docs.title: Code of Conduct
docs.text: Please adhere to the project's code of conduct when contributing. Be respectful and constructive in your interactions.

docs.title: Project Setup
docs.text: This document provides instructions for setting up the PowerCV project locally.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.10 or higher
  • Virtual environment tool (e.g., venv, poetry, or pipenv)
  • Docker (optional, for containerized development)

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository: bash git clone https://github.com/AnalyticAce/PowerCV.git cd PowerCV

  2. Create and activate a virtual environment: bash python -m venv venv source venv/bin/activate # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate

  3. Install dependencies: bash pip install -r requirements.txt

  4. Run the development server: bash python app/main.py

  5. Access the application at http://127.0.0.1:8000.

For Docker setup, refer to the Dockerfile and docker-compose documentation.
